title: A fixed PPG spectral filter lowers respiratory-rate error in two cohorts, but temporal-memory benefit remains unresolved
abstract: A fixed causal Gaussian grid filter lowered PPG respiratory-rate MAE versus independent-window arithmetic3 spectra by1.246 breaths/min (95%record-bootstrap CI0.756 to1.759) in BIDMC and1.097 (0.337 to2.041) in independent CapnoBase. However,benefit over a memoryless filter with identical boundary weighting was unresolved:0.194 (-0.257 to0.628) and0.408 (-0.227 to1.167). Thus temporal-memory-specific physiological information was not established. Both datasets were previously exposed;no clinical superiority or untouched confirmation is claimed. Author sensitivity checks found shuffled history no worse in BIDMC and a fixed18 Gaussian spectral prior substantially better there. Negative memory-specific evidence limits interpretation of apparent baseline gains.
